_README: MARKER-ONLY. Never fetched by the student's browser until a teacher/marker PDF is generated (formative: automatically when the student clicks Generate; assessed: only via the ?teacher=1-gated action, after Final Submit). Never render any of this on the student-facing page. See CLAUDE.md section 5's assessment-security amendment.

markingScheme.criterion: Describes the pattern using at least three of the student's own logged readings taken at different temperatures with the same water in the jar, quoting actual figures: as the air got colder the relative humidity rose (for example 30 C ~ 30%, 20 C ~ 55%, 10 C ~ 100%), while the dew point stayed the same.
markingScheme.accept: Any three genuine rows from the student's own Investigation Record showing RH rising as temperature falls AND the dew point staying (about) constant; approximate figures are fine. The student's 'My RH' or the instrument 'RH' column may be quoted.
markingScheme.insufficient: A general claim ('colder air has higher humidity') with no recorded figures from at least three of their own readings, or figures quoted for the temperature trend but nothing said about the dew point.

markingScheme.criterion: States clearly whether the evidence supported or refuted the hypothesis chosen before the experiment, explicitly referring to their own recorded data.
markingScheme.accept: Any judgement (supported / refuted / partially supported) that is consistent with what their own data actually shows and refers back to it. Students who chose option (a) should say it was supported.
markingScheme.insufficient: Repeating the hypothesis wording without saying whether the evidence agreed with it.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains, in terms of how much water vapour air can hold, why relative humidity changed but the dew point did not: colder air can hold less water vapour (its capacity falls) while the amount of vapour in the jar stayed the same, so the same vapour is a larger percentage of what the air can hold (RH rises); the dew point depends only on how much vapour is present, which has not changed.
markingScheme.accept: Equivalent wording, e.g. 'cold air is nearer to being full', 'the jar holds the same grams of water but the air can hold fewer grams', 'dew point is set by the amount of water vapour, so it only changes if water is added or removed'. Both halves must be present: why RH changes AND why the dew point does not.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying only that 'cold air holds less water' without connecting it to RH rising, or saying only that the dew point 'stays the same' without a reason.

markingScheme.criterion: Compares the dawn air temperature (9 C) with the dew point (8 C): the gap is only about 1 C, so the air is almost completely full of water vapour (relative humidity about 94%); the night cooled the air to its dew point, the air became saturated, and the excess water vapour condensed into tiny droplets - fog.
markingScheme.accept: Any statement that the temperature had cooled to (or very close to) the dew point so the air was saturated / at about 100% RH and vapour condensed. The 94% figure is not required.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying only 'it was cold so fog formed' without comparing temperature with the dew point or mentioning saturation.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains that warming to 18 C raises how much water vapour the air can hold (its capacity), while the amount of vapour (dew point 8 C) has not changed, so the relative humidity falls (to about 54%), the air is no longer saturated, and the fog droplets evaporate - the fog lifts.
markingScheme.accept: Any equivalent mechanism: warmer air can hold more vapour so it is no longer full, the droplets evaporate back into vapour. Mentioning that the dew point is unchanged because no water was added is a good sign but not required.
markingScheme.insufficient: 'The sun burns it off' or 'it gets hot' with no link to how much water vapour the warmer air can hold.

markingScheme.criterion: Finishes with a genuine evaluation sentence that names ONE specific way the real atmosphere differs from the sealed jar AND says how that could change what happens.
markingScheme.accept: e.g. wind moves air and moisture in or out (fog could persist or clear sooner); evaporation from the sea or ground adds water vapour; air at different heights mixes; air pressure changes with height; tiny particles in real air are needed for droplets to form. The effect on the outcome must be stated.
markingScheme.insufficient: A vague 'the real world is more complicated' with no named difference, or a named difference with no effect on the outcome.

criteria.source: Auto-marked from the Knowledge Check (auto_marked_score, kc1-kc4 = 1 + 4 + 1 + 1 = 7 marks; kc5 is an unscored reflection slider) - the teacher does not mark this row.

= the Explain question's 3-point marking scheme above, one-to-one (pattern from three of their own readings, hypothesis judgement, capacity/dew-point explanation). Do not award these 3 marks a second time here.

levels.descriptor: None of the three analytic points achieved: no use of own logged readings, no judgement on the hypothesis, and no capacity-based explanation.

Any one of the three analytic points achieved (the pattern quoted from at least three own readings; a supported/refuted judgement tied to the data; or the explanation that colder air holds less vapour while the dew point depends on the unchanged amount of vapour).
Any two of the three analytic points achieved.

All three analytic points achieved: quotes figures from at least three of their own readings showing RH rising and the dew point staying constant; states whether this supported the hypothesis; and explains why RH changed but the dew point did not in terms of how much vapour air can hold.

criteria.source: = the Apply question's 3-point marking scheme above, one-to-one (temperature vs dew point at dawn leading to fog, warming raising capacity so the fog lifts, evaluation of the jar model). Do not award these 3 marks a second time here.

levels.descriptor: None of the three analytic points achieved: no comparison of temperature with dew point, no explanation of the fog lifting, no evaluation of the model.

Any one of the three analytic points achieved (dawn temperature close to dew point so saturated and fog forms; warming raises capacity so RH falls and the fog evaporates; a named difference between the real atmosphere and the jar with its effect).
Any two of the three analytic points achieved.

All three analytic points achieved: compares 9 C with the 8 C dew point to explain saturation and fog; explains that warming raises how much vapour the air can hold so RH falls and the fog lifts; and names one real difference from the jar with its effect on the outcome.

criteria.source: Assessed holistically across both the Explain and Apply answers together - independent of, and never overlapping with, the content marks in use_of_evidence and reasoning above.

levels.descriptor: Too unclear or incomplete for the reasoning to be followed reliably, or key terms (temperature, dew point, relative humidity, water vapour, condensation) are missing or used incorrectly.
Main meaning understandable, but organisation or vocabulary has problems - for example confusing relative humidity with the amount of water vapour, or using 'humidity' with no qualifier.

Clear and logical, using correct vocabulary (dew point, relative humidity, saturation, water vapour, condensation) precisely enough to follow easily. Minor spelling or grammar slips do not cost a mark unless they harm meaning.

markingInstructions: Mark ONLY the two constructed responses (Explain, Apply). Award marks point-by-point using each question's marking_scheme in marking_context: each point is worth the marks stated, is independent unless it names a dependsOn point (in which case only award it if that earlier point was also awarded), and each point's 'accept'/'insufficient' tell you exactly what does and doesn't count. use_of_evidence's 3 marks ARE the Explain marking_scheme's 3 points, and reasoning's 3 marks ARE the Apply marking_scheme's 3 points - the rubric levels restate the same points as bands; award each set of 3 marks ONCE, not twice. communication is a separate, holistic 2 marks across both answers' clarity and vocabulary, never overlapping with the content marks. The Knowledge Check is already auto-marked in auto_marked_score (kc1-kc4; kc5 is an unscored reflection slider) - copy it into knowledge_accuracy (7 marks = full). Use the student's actual logged readings (the temp/dew/vapour/spec/rh/myrh/check/state columns in simulation_results.trials) to verify any figure they claim to quote - do not take their prose summary on trust if it does not match their own logged data. Note: the jar model is a simplified sealed rigid container using the Magnus approximation, so instrument RH and a student's table-based 'My RH' can differ by 1-3 percentage points; both are acceptable. Accept scientifically valid alternative wording per each point's 'accept' field, and do not penalise spelling unless meaning is unclear. Total is out of 15 (7 auto + 3 + 3 + 2); report the percentage, one strength, one correction, and one next step, in under 80 words.
